title: Presentability from monadicity and sifted colimits
statement: Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory and $\mathcal V$ a presentable infinity category. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$ is presentable. More generally, let $\mathcal C$ be any presentable infinity category and $F:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U$ a mapping-space adjunction of locally small infinity categories. Suppose $\mathcal D$ has all small sifted colimits, $U$ preserves them, and the comparison $\mathcal D\to\operatorname{Alg}_{UF}(\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence; here $UF$ is the coherent monad of the adjunction, and $\operatorname{Alg}_{UF}$ denotes its homotopy coherent algebra infinity category. Then $\mathcal D$ is presentable. Sifted means that indexed colimits in spaces commute with finite products. All smallness and presentability assertions use the fixed smaller universe; no equality between the presentability ranks of $\mathcal V$, $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ is asserted.
